entries.reason: iOS 6 carries no CIPremultiplyAlpha and no CIUnpremultiplyAlpha, and a colour matrix is linear over the four channels it is given, so no filter of the release scales a channel by the alpha of the same pixel. The matrix the port had here put the alpha into red, green and blue, which is a grey image of the alpha and not a premultiplied one: measured, the system renders 96 487584e5 with pixel 0 77 38 115 128 and the port rendered 96 fd3b7745 with pixel 0 128 128 128 128
entries.effect: nothing: respondsToSelector: answers NO, which is the truth on a release with no premultiply filter, and no caller gets a grey image where it asked for a premultiplied one
entries.source: the header of the iOS 16.4 SDK for the contract; the host's own CoreImage over the same call, by tests/backports/host/ciimage/pixel; the 6.1.3 armv7 dyld cache, which carries neither premultiply filter

entries.reason: iOS 6 carries no CIBlendWithAlphaMask and no kernel it can compile one from, so no filter of the release sets the alpha over part of an image. The implementation this row had put the image through CIBlendWithMask with a white field cropped to the rectangle and then a colour matrix, and it gave back a different shape and a different picture: measured over a field of 0.6 0.3 0.9 at alpha 0.5, the system answers extent 0 0 6 4 with pixels 96 7ded0a95 and pixel 0 77 38 115 255, and the port answered an infinite extent with pixels 96 b6ce03c5 and pixel 0 153 77 229 255 - the extent infinite because a white constant-colour generator is, and the picture the un-premultiplied colour where the system's is the premultiplied one
entries.effect: nothing: respondsToSelector: answers NO, which is the truth on a release with no alpha-over-a-region filter, and no caller gets an infinite image where it asked for one of the receiver's own extent
